title: Mass on a spring

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, narration or visual cue indicates slow motion; motion is a schematic animation

subjects.description: small green rectangular mass attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A green block hung from a vertical spring oscillates up and down above a black-and-white striped bar. It starts low near the bar and continues bouncing vertically for the whole clip without being caught or stopping.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The track is a straight vertical line with s spanning 0-210 pixels and period ~0.75s, slowly decaying peaks indicating light damping in air. Candidates go from ideal SHM to viscous damping to quadratic air drag and cubic spring nonlinearity to test loss and anharmonic effects on the held-back decay.

critique.finding: The green block bounces like a damped spring whose rest point slowly sinks, with tone {omega} around rest {s_eq} plus damping {gamma} and bend {beta} and sink {drift}. It only partly captures the motion and leaves a clear slow drift in its misses.
critique.headline: Spring block bounces with sinking rest and stiffening pull
critique.revision_idea: Let the rest position relax toward a limit instead of sliding forever, like creep that slows. The mean miss rises then falls again, showing constant-rate drift overshoots and then misses late.
critique.why_it_won: It alone lets the rest position slide with time, removing the large early-to-late tilt that swamps the plain damped and ideal springs.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add a slow drift in equilibrium position for spring creep or slipping support. Bin means climb steadily from low to high with near-perfect autocorrelation, showing the model sits low early and high late.

postRevision.revision_idea: Let the rest position relax toward a limit instead of sliding forever, like creep that slows. The mean miss rises then falls again, showing constant-rate drift overshoots and then misses late.
